limitations: Offline laboratory observation analysis; no production integration.
Node views are non-atomic and retained independently; sample timestamps are not exact server event times.
No fault labels, injected action results, run identifiers, configuration hashes or phase names are inference inputs.
Client reachability does not establish process death; no administrative process telemetry is accepted from fault-specific fields.
Validation proves only the recorded checked population, never general durability or power-loss safety.

hypotheses.description: Final acknowledged-value validation observed missing or corrupt values. Serving requests does not establish data preservation.
missing_evidence: Independent process liveness and network-path observations
verification_steps: Inspect independently collected process and network status
Compare all node views and client outcomes at aligned timestamps

recommendations.objective: Preserve evidence and investigate acknowledged-value validation failures
preconditions: Confirm affected node identity and current topology
Obtain operator approval before any state-changing action
Preserve logs and verify available backups
risks: Stale observations may identify the wrong current owner
Changing topology can lose data or interrupt availability
Rejoining or overwriting a node may destroy recoverable values
recommendations.expected_effects: Resolve alternative explanations without executing remediation
verification_criteria: Inspect independently collected process and network status
Compare all node views and client outcomes at aligned timestamps
Read the frozen acknowledged ledger and compare expected values; retain unreadable and unchecked counts

unresolved_uncertainty: Insufficient evidence to identify a unique root cause. Process failure, network disruption and observation-channel failure can be indistinguishable.
